title: Deferred-ACK failover for streamed request paths
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In active-active edge we observe either dropped or duplicated tokens during cross-region failover for long-lived streaming sessions. Current approaches (hard drain, immediate redirect) either violate our P95 streaming latency SLOs or cause duplicate model consumption and billing weirdness. Goal: design a gateway-level flow that enables safe, low-latency failover for streaming requests without double-issuing tokens to backends, and that degrades gracefully under overload with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies.
proposal_summary: Introduce a Deferred-ACK protocol in the gateway that defers final client ACK of a stream segment until a minimal backend commit/anchor is replicated to a lightweight KV lease. The model-serving runtime treats deferred-ack segments as tentatively committed; on failover a new replica can resume from last anchor without double-processing. Combine with adaptive circuit-breakers that raise deferred-ack windows under high headroom and reduce during overload. The approach reduces cross-region roundtrips during normal operation and bounds duplication risk during failover.
rationale_and_tradeoffs: Consistency vs latency: deferred-ACK reduces risk of duplication but increases window where a request is tentatively accepted; we bound this window to 1-3 segments (configurable) to keep perceived latency low.
Cost: requires lightweight KV writes per anchor (small payloads). We expect 0.1-0.5% increase in token-unit cost vs baseline but significant reduction in failover-induced replays.
Complexity: adds gateway-to-KV path and small state-machine per stream. Prefer implementation in edge gateway process to avoid cross-service coordination where possible.
Failure modes: KV unavailability falls back to optimistic immediate-ack with heightened duplication detection and billing attribution flags.
Security: anchor metadata must avoid including PII; security review flagged to ensure no request bodies are stored.
Compatibility: backward-compatible with existing streaming client SDKs; client receives same stream chunks with an extra ack/commit event optional header for new SDKs.
Observability: requires new metrics (anchor_latency_ms, deferred_ack_window, anchor_failures) and traces linking stream chunk -> anchor write -> model token generation.
Alternatives considered: sticky-region sessions, full state replication, proxy-level session locks. Deferred-ACK chosen for best latency/SLO balance and operational simplicity.
Open question: precise anchor frequency vs token budget for high-throughput short-chunk streams — experiment needed.
acceptance_criteria: Gateways can emit anchor writes to KV within 50ms P95 under normal load in primary region.
Failover reproduction test: when region A fails, region B resumes streaming sessions from last anchor with <1% duplicated tokens in replay test.
SLO compliance: end-to-end P95 streaming latency increases by no more than 10% compared to baseline for 95% of test traffic.
Circuit-breaker: gateway exposes adaptive circuit state and reduces deferred-ack window to 0 when headroom < 5%.
Automated integration tests cover anchor write loss and fallback path.
Confluence design doc and security review completed and linked.
Rollout plan exists with canary percentage steps and telemetry dashboards configured.
Documentation: release notes and SDK optional header docs published.
Cost impact analysis reviewed by finance and product (cost delta <= 1% for typical workloads).
Runbook: failover recovery and incident playbook updated in operations playbooks.
PRs merged for gateway changes and runtime resume logic; release cut in runtime-1.20.

progress_updates: 2026-03-15: Spike completed. Prototype gateway attaches anchor metadata to stream chunks and writes to KV async; observed median anchor write 12ms in dev cluster.
2026-03-18: Design review with Runtime team. Runtime asks for compact anchor format (8-12 bytes) and idempotency token to avoid reprocessing on resume.
2026-03-20: Security flagged need to strip user prompt fragments from anchor. Proposal updated to include only sequence ids and model state digest (no user content).

2026-03-24: Interim decision: implement local ephemeral anchor cache in gateway that periodically flushes to global KV; on failover, connecting region consults last-known cluster-local anchors then global KV; this reduces write latency but increases recovery complexity (recorded in tradeoffs).

2026-03-30: Canary plan drafted with telemetry gates (anchor_latency_p95 < 60ms AND duplicate_replays < 1%).

risks_and_mitigation: KV hotspotting when many gateways anchor simultaneously: mitigation - staggered flush windows and local batching with jitter.
Increased tail latency during anchor writes: mitigation - local cache fallback and backpressure signals to clients (optional), and adaptive window shrink under load.
Edge crash after local anchor but before global flush: mitigation - periodic durable checkpointing and resume from nearest region with cross-region sync within bounded T.
Operational complexity during rollout: mitigation - gradual canary, strong telemetry, runbook and rollback conditions defined.
Billing attribution confusion for rare duplicates: mitigation - flag duplicates and tie to canary window; billing team to provide credits for affected customers during rollout.
SDK compatibility: mitigation - preserve current behavior for old SDKs; new header is optional and backward compatible.
